  • Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the concern could occur by Wednesday.
  • A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., conducts a news conference outside the Capitol on Monday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., took to the House floor Monday to unveil a resolution that would impeach Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth, and a vote on the concern could occur by Wednesday.

A draft resolution that Massie read aloud on the House floor on Monday accused Hegseth of eight violations of law or the Constitution, including that he violated the 1973 War Powers Resolution in his prosecution of the Iran war and acted illegally in military campaigns in Venezuela, Yemen, the Caribbean Sea and the eastern Pacific Ocean.

Sources indicate that massie's resolution also charges Hegseth with disregarding protection of civilians in wartime and suppressing the free speech of a U.S. senator.

Massie confirmed his intention to file the resolution as a matter of the privileges of the House.

Recent findings suggest that speaker Mike Johnson, R-La., will now have to rule as to whether the resolution constitutes a proper question of the privileges of the House. There is precedent from prior instances when impeachment was found to be valid as it relates to the House’s constitutionally granted powers.

It has been revealed that he must schedule a vote to occur within two legislative days. Assuming that the speaker rules that Massie's resolution is privileged, the House could vote on the resolution itself, or on a motion to table it or refer it to committee.

Sources indicate that if the House were to impeach Hegseth under this process, it would mark a historical anomaly. According to the Congressional Research Service, recent attempts to impeach an official as a matter of the privileges of the House have not resulted in approval of the resolution. In cases in which an official has been impeached, the House has nearly always chosen to conduct an investigation first.

Sources indicate that in an interview on Oct. 26, Massie put the chances of his resolution being adopted at 50-50.

In comments to reporters outside the Capitol after his floor remarks, Massie mentioned he suspected some Republicans may back his resolution but he indicated he has neither asked for nor received any such assurances from any of them.

Sources indicate that he predicted there could be some GOP support in the Senate if Hegseth is impeached and it goes to trial. He noted that if the trial does not start until 2027, any Republicans who might vote to convict Hegseth would presumably be joined by most if not all of a more sizeable Senate Democratic caucus.

Massie's odds of success for his resolution may now be greater than his previous 50-50 prediction given the results of the Nov. 3 midterm elections, which gave Democrats control over both chambers in the next Congress — a vote motivated largely by opposition to the Iran war and its inflationary impact.

According to recent reports, the questions now are, first, how many House Republicans will defy President Donald Trump and vote to impeach Hegseth; and, secondly, how many incumbents who lost their reelection bids on Nov. 3, a cohort that is disproportionately Republican, might be absent for the impeachment vote?

Massie said some Republicans who lost their reelection bids may feel freer to vote to impeach Hegseth. And he also said Republicans who were reelected and will have to face voters in 2028 may also think about how their vote on an impeachment resolution would reverberate politically.

"It's going to be everybody's conscience, and then they'll have to live with that vote," Massie noted. "And they're going to have to live with that vote two years from now if they're not part of the retirement caucus. And if they were part of the retirement caucus, what do they have to lose?".

Asked why he did not bring articles of impeachment against President Donald Trump, Massie said: "I think the president needs to see one of — this is a metaphor — one of his horses shot out from under him, and then maybe he'll he will see things differently.".

If the House does vote on Massie’s resolution, Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., who is expected to become the House speaker in the next Congress, stated on ABC’s “This Week” on Sunday that he would be a “hard yes” on it.

Hegseth has “got to go,” Jeffries stated. “The so-called secretary of Defense has abused his power, undermined our national security and engineered this reckless and costly war of choice in Iran, which has skyrocketed prices on the American people and made the country less safe.”.

Most if not all House Democrats are expected to agree.

Last week, Rep. Adam Smith, D-Wash., the ranking member of the Armed Services Committee and its likely chairman in the next Congress, indicated in an interview with The New Republic that he would support Massie’s impeachment resolution, and he predicted it would be adopted.

Referring to Massie’s measure, Smith noted, “By every estimation, it will pass and he will be impeached. And off that goes to the Senate. Then the Senate is legally required to spend all of their time dealing with that until it’s done with.”.

Industry observers note that "Every second Pete Hegseth remains at the top of the Pentagon, our servicemembers are at risk," Rep. Jason Crow, D-Colo., a senior member of the Armed Services Committee, remarked in a post on X on Sunday.

Recent findings suggest that also on Monday, Everett B. Kelley, the national president of the American Federation of Government Employees, a union that represents some 820,000 federal and D.C. government employees, sent a letter to House members urging a “yes” vote on Massie's Hegseth impeachment resolution.

The letter cited the risks Kelley said the Iran war has posed to the lives of the Defense Department's uniformed and civilian personnel, and the missive noted Hegseth's stripping of workplace rights and protections for the department's civilians.

In a recent development, "By adopting Rep. Massie’s resolution, the House can begin the long overdue bipartisan effort to reclaim its constitutional powers and authority, restore checks and balances, and take responsibility for the lives of military personnel and civilian employees that Mr. Hegseth’s capricious leadership has jeopardized," Kelley wrote.

Massie declared in mid-September his intention to file an impeachment resolution against Hegseth. But Johnson adjourned the House before the vote would have occurred.

Massie’s fresh resolution is substantially the same as his earlier one, with the same eight articles of impeachment.

The first three of these alleges that Hegseth’s conduct of the Iran war violated the War Powers Resolution.

Massie's measure states Hegseth prosecuted the Iran war without congressional authorization and in the absence of an attack on the United States or an imminent threat.

According to recent reports, further, the measure alleges that Hegseth continued the war despite the House and Senate adopting in June a concurrent war powers resolution calling for the withdrawal of U.S. forces from the fight.

And, the resolution says, Hegseth continued the Iran war after the expiration of the War Powers Resolution’s 60-day termination period and any potential 30-day withdrawal period.

Massie’s measure further asserts that Hegseth:.

Industry observers note that the House has only voted twice to impeach a member of the Cabinet. In 1876, Secretary of War William Belknap was impeached over allegations of corruption, and his abrupt resignation likely contributed to his acquittal in the Senate.

In 2024, the House voted 214-213 to impeach Alejandro Mayorkas, then-secretary of Homeland Security, for “willful and systemic refusal to comply with the law” and “breach of public trust.” The Senate dispensed with the charges without a trial.

Tech Report: Airport Luggage Tag Scam: How to Protect Your Checked Bags in 2026

📅 14 Jun 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Theplanetd

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Imagine walking up to customs after a long international flight and being told that a suitcase connected to your name has been flagged.
  • Then the officer points to the luggage tag and says, “Then why is your name on it?”.
  • In a recent development, that is the nightmare behind a luggage scam travelers need to understand in 2026.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Imagine walking up to customs after a long international flight and being told that a suitcase connected to your name has been flagged.

Then the officer points to the luggage tag and says, “Then why is your name on it?”.

In a recent development, that is the nightmare behind a luggage scam travelers need to understand in 2026. It is called baggage tag switching, and it is exactly what it sounds like: the luggage tag from an innocent passenger’s checked suitcase is allegedly removed and placed onto another bag.

Baggage tag switching scams happen when the luggage tag from a traveler’s checked bag is allegedly removed and placed on another suitcase. To protect yourself, take a video of your suitcase before check-in, photograph the bag on the scale, take a close-up photo of the baggage tag, keep your baggage receipt, place a tracker inside your suitcase, and report any damaged, missing, delayed, or retagged bag before leaving the airport.

Sources indicate that according to a W5 investigation, innocent passengers flying from Canada have been detained after their real luggage tags were allegedly moved onto suitcases containing illegal drugs. The investigation focused on flights from Canada and alleged cases connected to Toronto Pearson, but the larger lesson applies to travelers everywhere: once your checked bag disappears behind the counter, you are trusting the system to protect your luggage, your tag, and your name.

We have traveled to more than 130 countries on all seven continents, and checked bags have always been part of travel. But the old habit of simply handing over your suitcase and hoping for the best needs an update.

In 2026, protecting your checked luggage is not just about stopping theft. It is about protecting the paper trail that connects you to your bag.

This is part of a bigger shift in how travelers need to think about airport safety, baggage scams, and common airport security mistakes before they fly.

Editor’s note: This article is based on our video about baggage tag switching, which has reached more than 86,000 views on our travel YouTube channel.

Before you check a bag, take two minutes to create proof that the bag is yours.

It also helps to run through a full pre-travel checklist before you leave for the airport so you are not rushing through check-in.

Recent findings suggest that this may sound like a lot, but it takes less than two minutes at check-in. And those two minutes could matter if your name ever gets attached to a suitcase that is not yours.

We covered this luggage tag scam in detail in the video below, including the simple two-minute routine we now recommend before checking a bag.

Baggage tag switching is when the tag printed for your checked luggage is removed from your actual suitcase and attached to another bag.

It has been revealed that when you check luggage, the airline prints a baggage tag that usually includes your name, flight, destination, routing information, barcode, and bag number. That tag is the airport system’s way of connecting that suitcase to you.

The problem is that once your bag goes behind the counter, you cannot see what happens next.

Sources indicate that in the alleged scheme reported by W5, corrupt baggage or ramp workers could remove a legitimate tag from a passenger’s suitcase and attach it to another suitcase heading to the same destination. If that second bag is intercepted, the paperwork points back to the innocent passenger.

That is what makes this scam so dangerous. You may have done everything right: checked your own suitcase, kept your boarding pass, and boarded your flight. But behind the scenes, one strip of paper may now connect your name to a bag you have never seen.

Most airport workers are honest. Let’s be clear about that. The vast majority are doing hard jobs under pressure, moving thousands of bags through complex systems every day. But a baggage system only needs a few bad actors to create a very serious problem.

This story has received attention because of Canadian cases, but this is not only a Canada problem.

The bigger glitch is that every major airport has the same basic weak point: you hand over your suitcase, it enters a restricted area, and from that point on, you are relying on the system to protect the tag, the bag, and the records connected to your name.

That is true in Toronto. It is true in New York, London, Paris, Dubai, Bangkok, Mexico City, Sydney, and anywhere else checked luggage moves behind the scenes.

It has been revealed that international travel also adds another layer of risk. If your name gets tied to a suspicious bag in another country, you may be dealing with a different legal system, different customs procedures, and possibly a language barrier.

It has been revealed that the Government of Canada warns travelers that drug offences abroad can have serious consequences and that you should never carry anything across a border for someone else. The Canada Border Services Agency also specifically reminds travelers that trafficking cannabis or other drugs across the border is a criminal offence and warns people to beware of anyone asking them to carry something.

That is why documenting your own luggage matters. You are not being paranoid. You are creating a simple evidence trail.

Before your suitcase disappears behind the counter, take a clear video of it.

Do a full 360-degree view. Show the front, back, sides, wheels, handles, color, brand, straps, stickers, scratches, dents, or anything that makes your bag identifiable.

Yes, you may feel ridiculous filming your suitcase at the airport. Do it anyway. People film lattes. You can film the thing that might keep you out of a holding room.

It has been revealed that this video creates a time-stamped record of what your suitcase looked like before it left your hands. If someone later claims a different bag is yours, you have proof of what your actual luggage looked like at check-in.

When your bag is placed on the airline scale, take a quick photo or video showing the weight.

Industry observers note that this matters because weight is part of the paper trail. If your suitcase weighed 19 kilograms at check-in and another suitcase connected to your name weighs 32 kilograms, that difference may matter.

Industry observers note that you are not trying to become a detective. You are simply creating a record that says this was your bag, this was the weight, this was the condition, and this was the tag attached to it.

That is the kind of simple documentation that can help if your bag is delayed, damaged, retagged, or questioned later.

Once the airline attaches the baggage tag to your suitcase, take a close-up photo or video of it before the bag goes onto the conveyor belt.

Make sure you can clearly see the barcode, destination airport, flight number, routing, and bag number. Also check that the airline has looped and attached the tag properly.

In a recent development, you are not being difficult. You are checking the one strip of paper connecting you to your luggage. That little tag is doing a lot of legal heavy lifting.

Air Canada’s own baggage information explains that self-service kiosks can print baggage tags, receipts, and boarding passes, and that travelers then attach the tags and proceed to bag drop. That means passengers are often handling or reviewing this paperwork themselves before the bag disappears into the system.

Never throw away the little baggage receipt sticker you receive at check-in.

Keep it somewhere safe. Don’t stuff it in a random pocket, lose it before boarding, or assume the airline app is enough. Put it with your passport or travel documents until your suitcase is back in your hands.

It has been revealed that that receipt usually contains your bag number. If something goes wrong, that number becomes part of the evidence trail. That number can help airline staff or investigators compare what you checked, what arrived, and whether someone intercepted or retagged another bag.

This is one of the easiest travel habits to fix, and it costs nothing.

Before you close your checked bag, take one clear photo of the inside.

You do not need to photograph every sock like you are filing a museum inventory. Just take one clear photo of the contents: clothes, shoes, toiletries, chargers, jackets, and the usual chaos of travel.

This helps show what you actually packed. If a suitcase connected to your name contains items you have never seen, you have a record of what was inside your real bag before check-in.

This is especially useful on international trips, where proving what you packed may become more complicated once you are outside your home country.

It is also a good reminder to double-check what not to pack in checked luggage before you leave for the airport.

A luggage tracker will not stop someone from tampering with a baggage tag, but it can help show where your real suitcase went.

We use Apple AirTags, but there are also Tile trackers, Samsung SmartTags, and other luggage tracking options.

The important thing is this: put the tracker inside your suitcase. Do not hang it outside where it can easily be removed.

If authorities are asking about a suitcase connected to your name and your tracker shows your actual suitcase is somewhere else, that becomes another part of your evidence trail.

Recent findings suggest that trackers are also helpful if your bag arrives late, gets separated from its original tag, or ends up in the wrong baggage area. They are not perfect, but they give travelers one more layer of information when airline systems fail.

We use AirTags in our checked bags, but Samsung SmartTags and Tile trackers are also good options depending on your phone. The key is to keep the tracker inside the suitcase where it cannot easily be removed.

We also recommend pairing a luggage tracker with a few simple anti-theft travel accessories especially on longer international trips.

A plain black suitcase is basically the airport version of camouflage.

Make your luggage easier to identify with a bright strap, ribbon, sticker, or distinctive luggage tag. You want to be able to spot your bag swiftly and prove what makes it different from hundreds of others.

Industry observers note that but do not put too much personal information on the outside. Your name and phone number are enough.

You do not need your home address waving around the baggage hall like an invitation that notes, “Please rob us while we’re in Italy.”.

Keep luggage identifiable, but not overly revealing.

This rule has always mattered, but it matters even more now.

In a recent development, never carry a package, gift, suitcase, envelope, or item for someone else. That means no favors for strangers, no “harmless” packages, and no quick airport errands for someone you barely know.

If you did not pack it, you do not carry it.

The CBSA specifically warns travelers to beware of people who ask them to carry anything and notes that consequences for drug trafficking can be serious in Canada and abroad.

That is the cleanest rule in travel: your bag, your responsibility.

If your checked bag arrives without the original tag, with a damaged tag, with a rush tag, or through a different baggage process than expected, do not just shrug and leave the airport.

Do not rely on a quick conversation at the counter. Conversations disappear the second you walk away. Written reports create a record.

This matters if your bag was mishandled, delayed, retagged, or separated from its original tag.

When your suitcase comes out at baggage claim, do not grab it on autopilot and leave.

Check that it is actually yours. Look at the tag, compare the bag number against your receipt, check your tracker, inspect the condition, and make sure the contents have not obviously been disturbed.

We have seen people accidentally walk away with someone else’s luggage. It happens more easily than people think, especially after long-haul flights when everyone is tired and half the carousel is filled with identical black suitcases.

Before you leave the airport or customs area, take one minute to confirm everything looks right.

Recent findings suggest that not necessarily. We have traveled for decades, and carry-on only is not always realistic. Sometimes you need to check a bag, especially on longer trips, family trips, cruises, cold-weather destinations, camera-heavy travel, or extended international travel.

For a smoother trip overall, our easy air travel tips can help before you even reach baggage claim.

For longer flights, our long-haul flight tips can also help make the journey easier before you even get to baggage claim.

Sources indicate that the point is not to scare people out of checking luggage. The point is to update your habits.

The old way of checking luggage was simple: check the bag, keep the receipt somewhere, and hope for the best.

It sounds like a lot, but it takes less than two minutes — and those two minutes could make a huge difference if your name ever gets attached to a suitcase that is not yours.

If authorities ever question you about a suitcase that you do not recognize, stay calm.

Do not guess, don’t joke and do not become argumentative.

Ask for legal assistance and show the documentation you collected: your suitcase video, scale photo, baggage tag photo, receipt, tracker information, and photos of what you packed.

This article is not legal advice, but from a traveler’s perspective, the goal is simple: create proof before there is a problem.

If your name is ever attached to a bag you did not pack, your documentation may help show what your real suitcase looked like, what it weighed, what was inside it, and where it went.

Before every checked bag disappears behind the counter, take two minutes to create a simple record of your suitcase.

Recent findings suggest that that’s it. Two minutes. No drama. No paranoia. Just smart travel.

In a recent development, most airport workers are honest, and most checked bags arrive without a problem. But airport systems are massive, complicated, and not completely invisible-proof. Once your bag disappears behind the counter, you are trusting a chain of people, machines, tags, scans, and systems to keep your suitcase connected to your name.

That is usually fine — until it is not.

Sources indicate that so before your next flight, take two minutes to protect yourself. Film your bag. Photograph your tag. Keep your receipt. Use a tracker. And never carry anything for anyone else.

It has been revealed that the goal is not to travel scared. The goal is to travel smarter.

Because when travelers get smarter, scams get riskier for the people trying to pull them off.

Oceania Cruises has unveiled a upcoming Chef’s Studio aboard the Oceania Marina, introducing a venue for culinary education, destination discovery and chef-hosted experiences at sea.

Beginning November 25, 2026, the venue will welcome guests for a fresh series of culinary workshops, seminars and test kitchen experiences.

“Since introducing the first hands-on cooking school at sea aboard the Oceania Marina, Oceania Cruises has continually evolved the ways guests can connect with destinations through food and culture,” noted Jason Montague, chief luxury officer of Oceania Cruises.

“The fresh Chef’s Studio complements The Culinary Center while offering a different style of culinary enrichment, allowing guests to explore technique and the importance of linking place, history and gastronomy.”.

Debuting following the Oceania Marina’s extensive bow-to-stern refurbishment in October, the Chef’s Studio builds on the ship’s pioneering culinary legacy.

Designed for 18 guests, the Chef’s Studio offers a new perspective on learning opportunities with a roster of seminars, workshops and destination-focused discussions led by Chef Instructors, the company said in a press release.

The company stated that the venue’s new Test Kitchen Series features one-hour classes offered on sea days for $49 per person.

It is designed for travelers seeking a deeper understanding of food and culture.

Sessions focus on techniques and culinary fundamentals with topics ranging from The Spice of Life, knife skills, pantry organization and cooking with high heat to destination-inspired classes exploring regional ingredients, traditions and culinary practices from around the world.

The Chef’s Studio also serves as the gathering place for Oceania Cruises’ signature Culinary Discovery Tours.

According to the press release, guests meet before these small-group tours for an orientation and overview, and once the tour returns, guests and the chef return to the Chef’s Studio for a glass of wine to continue conversations and ask follow-up questions.

In 2027, Oceania Cruises expects to offer more than 100 chef-led Culinary Discovery Tours in destinations spanning Iceland, Australia, Uruguay and beyond.

The Chef’s Studio program will expand next year and debut aboard the Oceania Riviera and the line’s latest additions to the fleet, the Oceania Sonata and Oceania Aurelia.

Tech Report: How the ‘blue tsunami’ crested in North Carolina

📅 09 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1606 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Sources indicate that north Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for new member orientation.
  • LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.
  • But as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that north Carolina Rep.-elect LaKesha Womack talks to reporters Sunday at the AC Hotel in Washington as she arrives for new member orientation. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

LaKesha Womack faced towering odds as an underfunded Democrat making her first run for public office in a North Carolina district that Donald Trump carried by 15 points two years ago.

But as early voting surged in mid-October, she sensed she might pull off an upset over Republican Rep. Tim Moore, the influential former speaker of the North Carolina House and a chief architect of the gerrymander that aimed to keep the 14th District safely red.

Sources indicate that “There were a lot of pins and needles,” said Womack, a 49-year-old ordained minister who works at a Charlotte-based nonprofit. After seeing long lines at polling places extend into Election Day, she grew more confident: “People were ready to exercise their voice.”.

Womack – who raised less than $60,000 to Moore’s $2.1 million – eked out a 2-point win in the district, which reaches from the Charlotte suburbs to mountain counties in the west.

Recent findings suggest that saddled with an unpopular president and broad dissatisfaction with the status quo, Republican incumbents across the nation experienced a midterm drubbing last week. As of Monday evening, House Democrats had netted 42 seats, with more races left to be called. The GOP in North Carolina, a state that Trump carried three times, was among the hardest hit.

Democrats have so far flipped five House seats in the Tar Heel State. Besides Womack, the “blue tsunami” also swept in Paul Barringer, a lawyer who founded an outdoor clothing line, and High Point Mayor Cyril Jefferson. And Army veteran Richard Ojeda, who once served in the West Virginia Senate, defeated Rep. Richard Hudson, the chairman of the National Republican Congressional Committee.

Democrats also won two races that had been seen as competitive for much of the cycle. Farmer Jamie Ager flipped an open seat in the state’s mountain west, while Rep. Don Davis held on to his Eastern North Carolina district, which Republicans had redrawn in their favor.

Meanwhile, in the state’s hilly northwest corner, 11-term Republican Virginia Foxx, the chairwoman of the powerful Rules Committee, is fighting for her political future: As of Monday afternoon, former journalist Chuck Hubbard led her by 99 votes in the 5th District, though The Associated Press had yet to call the race.

That was also true in the neighboring 10th District, where GOP incumbent Pat Harrigan had a 1-point edge over Democratic physician associate Ashley Bell. Also uncalled were a pair of contests in Eastern North Carolina, where Republican Rep. Greg Murphy clung to a 233-vote edge over Democratic former state Rep. Raymond Smith and GOP Rep. David Rouzer led Democratic social worker Kimberly Hardy by less than a point.

According to recent reports, “Nobody could have predicted this,’’ said David Wilson Brown, who leads the Democratic Party in Gaston County near Charlotte and has lost two bids for the House, including to Foxx in 2020. “It’s a watershed moment.”.

The Democratic rout in the midterm elections was powered by victories in states with upcoming GOP-favored maps, including Texas, Ohio and Florida.

Recent findings suggest that but Democrats’ success in North Carolina was especially striking given the steep structural disadvantages the party faced. Since Republicans flipped the state legislature in 2010, and with it control of the redistricting process, no House GOP incumbent had lost a general election in the Tar Heel State until last week.

This year’s  congressional map – the state's sixth in seven election cycles – was engineered by the Republican-led legislature to help the party capture 11 of the state's 14 House seats.

Sources indicate that but the Democratic surge was so big that it easily overpowered the GOP’s built-in edge. Democratic candidates were also lifted by former Gov. Roy Cooper, whose 20-point Senate win provided the underticket with powerful coattails.

“In order for them to gerrymander our state in the way that they did, they were spread very thin,” Brown remarked, referring to state Republicans. “So they were kind of ripe to be defeated that way.”.

The repeated rounds of redistricting may have also erased some of the advantages of incumbency, according to Peter L. Francia, a political science professor at East Carolina University. “If you carve up a district every two years, you've taken away some of that [advantage]. And I think that that came back and hurt Republicans in this cycle.”.

Doug Heye, a GOP strategist and a former spokesman for the Republican National Committee, said redistricting “ticked off a whole lot of voters, and really activated the Democratic base.”.

On the Republican side, voters were “less motivated because they were unexcited about Trump,’’ Heye added.

Republican incumbents accustomed to winning by comfortable margins weren’t prepared for a political environment driven by anger over the war in Iran and angst about the rising cost of living.

“Clearly, a lot of those Republicans didn’t take their elections seriously,” Heye said. “They won last time with 18 points. They weren't on anyone's radar screen, so they didn't think they had to do anything.”.

Womack credits her win to a grassroots campaign centered on economic complications. While her race wasn’t on the national radar – Moore, after all, won by 16 points in 2024 – and her campaign didn’t have money for ads, she was out in the district doing events every day.

“There are a lot of working families right now who are in the missing middle,” she mentioned in an interview. “They make too much money to get help, but they don't make enough money to get ahead. … Someone who can be working a full-time job, but still doesn’t have enough money to buy groceries or to afford their medications or to have access to health insurance.”.

Womack said her own struggles have shaped her approach to politics. This week, she’s slated to appear in court on a felony charge for allegedly failing to return a rental car in 2019. The incident wound up in one of Moore’s attack ads.

“There are so many people who [understand] what happens when you're down on your luck and you don't have enough money to make good financial decisions,’’ she said. “Most people don't want those bad decisions to be a definition of their character for the rest of their life.”.

Early in the midterm cycle, Democratic opposition research group American Bridge prepared detailed dossiers on Republican House incumbents in North Carolina.

Recent findings suggest that “Someone like Virginia Foxx, she’s been on the Hill forever,” said Pat Dennis, the group’s president. “She was somebody … who under the radar could be vulnerable. So we started really early.”.

American Bridge’s political arm spent $340,000 on ads targeting Foxx. One spot featured a man who identified himself as a Trump voter expressing anger at the government’s response to Hurricane Helene, which devastated the mountain communities of Western North Carolina two years ago.

Other Democrats scoffed at the group’s decision to spend money targeting entrenched Republicans far from the main House battleground.

“There was a lot of reluctance from people to really believe that that data was correct, but it was,’’ Dennis stated. “Then over the summer, we saw her numbers collapsing, so we put paid media behind it and it really paid off.”.

Hubbard ran against Foxx two years ago and lost by almost 20 points.

“I kind of had a notion I was going to do this again,’’ he said in an interview Saturday while en route to Washington for freshman orientation. “I don’t like to lose at checkers, much less a congressional race.”.

After a court-drawn map resulted in a split North Carolina delegation after the 2022 elections, state Republicans won back control of the map-making process and went on to win 10 of the state’s 14 House seats under a new map two years later.

At Trump’s urging, Republicans made further tweaks to the North Carolina map last year, but the original gerrymander finally came back to bite the GOP in 2026, according to Hubbard.

Sources indicate that “North Carolina is one of the most severely gerrymandered states,’’ he remarked. “And what happened was they had to steal from Peter to pay Paul. It's been referred to by political scientists as a dummymander.”.

As the vote count in the 5th District continues, Foxx, whose campaign declined to comment for this story, has requested the presence of nonpartisan election observers.

They “will serve as notable, watchful eyes to ensure that this sacred process is not impeded and that all legal votes are counted in a consistent, thorough manner,’’ she posted on social media.

But even before the final races are called, Republicans are already looking to the next election.

According to recent reports, heye, who expects North Carolina to remain a purple state in 2028 and beyond, cautioned the Democrats who won last week not to get too comfortable in Washington. He invoked Fred Heineman, the former Raleigh police chief who rode the 1994 “Republican Revolution” to Congress – and lasted a single term.

“Some of them will lose, and some of the people who lost may run two years from now and get their seat back,’’ he said.

One GOP operative, who requested anonymity to speak candidly, offered up a similar assessment.

Trump “didn't keep his promises” and that “just got voters very angry and suppressed the GOP base from coming out because, in a midterm election it's a base turnout contest,’’ the strategist remarked.

“But these Democrats are renting these districts for two years.”.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Marella Cruises is expanding its regional flying program for the winter season, enabling guests to spend Christmas holidays sailing the Caribbean while flying from Newcastle.

Thanks to a direct TUI Airways flight to La Romana, Dominican Republic, departing Newcastle Airport on December 15, 2026, guests can sail a 14-night Caribbean fly-cruise that combines the “Colors of the Caribbean” and “A Caribbean Christmas” itineraries aboard the Marella Discovery.

They can also prolong their stay by combining the “Colors of the Caribbean” itinerary with a one week stay post-cruise at a choice of TUI hotels in La Romana.

“We’re delighted to be expanding our regional flying program from Newcastle Airport for Winter 2026, giving customers across the North East even more choice when it comes to starting their Caribbean holiday closer to home,” stated Chris Hackney, CEO at Marella Cruises.

“Regional flying is incredibly vital to us at Marella Cruises and the additional La Romana flying means customers can enjoy the convenience of departing from their local airport before experiencing everything our all-inclusive cruises and cruise and stay program has to offer.”.

The itinerary sailing roundtrip from La Romana calls at Roseau, Dominica; St John’s, Antigua; Basseterre, St Kitts; Philipsburg, St Maarten and Road Town, British Virgin Islands during the first week.

The second week visits Isla Catalina, an island off the Dominican Republic; Kralendijk, Bonaire; Willemstad, Curacao; Oranjestad, Aruba before returning to La Romana.

Prices start from £2,868 per person, based on two adults sharing a balcony cabin.

Leon McQuaid, director of aviation development at Newcastle Airport, noted: “Spending Christmas in the Caribbean is on many people’s bucket list, so it’s fantastic that passengers can make that dream a reality with direct flights from Newcastle Airport.

“Marella Cruises’ expanded program makes it easier than ever to swap the cold winter weather for Caribbean sunshine and stunning beaches, while exploring the region’s most spectacular islands.”.

Industry News: Scientists Studied Thousands of Ancient Skeletons and Found a Strange Truth About Human Progress

📅 20 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (769 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Popularmechanics

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, the dairy industry’s “Milk.
  • “When children and adolescents have access to sufficient, high-quality food, they grow taller, within the constraints of genetic factors,” Manon Stephan, an economic historian at Germany’s University of Tübingen, said in a statement.
  • Sources indicate that to test that idea, Stephan and colleagues at Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology examined 18,457 bones from 783 sites in 45 countries.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, the dairy industry’s “Milk. It does a body good” slogan has some historical backing, at least in Europe. That’s one of the more surprising takeaways from a large study that used ancient skeletons to track how well people lived across Europe and Asia over the past 7,000 years. The researchers based their analysis on one telling measurement: human height.

“When children and adolescents have access to sufficient, high-quality food, they grow taller, within the constraints of genetic factors,” Manon Stephan, an economic historian at Germany’s University of Tübingen, said in a statement. “Therefore, height enables us to draw conclusions about living standards.”.

Sources indicate that to test that idea, Stephan and colleagues at Tübingen and the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology examined 18,457 bones from 783 sites in 45 countries. In the study, published in Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences, the team estimated people’s heights from their long bones. They then tracked how average height changed in each region and compared those changes with shifts in population density and technology.

According to recent reports, in China, men were taller 7,000 years ago, averaging 5 feet 10 inches. Over time, however, their height steadily declined, reaching a low of just 5 feet 3 inches on average in the 19th century. Chinese women’s height also declined, though less drastically, falling from an average of 5 feet 2 inches 7,000 years ago to 4 feet 10 inches in more recent times.

Recent findings suggest that trends like these would be nearly impossible to trace through written records alone. “In many parts of the world, any written sources that would allow us to draw conclusions about economic development appear quite late on our timeline and are patchy in their distribution,” Stephan noted. “That’s why we rely on bones.” The bones in question came from 22 Asian and 23 European countries and were taken from the graves of commoners in both densely populated and rural regions.

In Europe, by contrast, the trends went in a different direction. Around 5,000 years ago, men in northern Europe averaged just 5 feet 4 inches. However, the study authors wrote, as pastoralist peoples migrated from the steppes of Eastern Europe and western Siberia, they brought with them more advanced dairy farming and the genetic trait of lactose tolerance. This led to greater consumption of dairy products, which the study identifies as a leading factor in increased height. Average heights in northern Europe continued to climb into the early Middle Ages, but sometime between 500 and 1000 C.E., they began to decline, a trend that lasted until the end of the 19th century.

Women’s heights followed a similar pattern. China and Japan experienced the steepest declines, while Europe saw a rise, though a less steep one than among men.

According to recent reports, the authors wrote that “human stature is a valuable indicator of nutritional status and health.” Reconstructing this indicator offers insight into which societies provided better health and nutrition to their people. Surprisingly, technological progress did not prove to be a major factor in improving either.

“Our study also confirmed that technological progress does not automatically lead to greater height,” noted Jörg Baten, a professor of economic history at the University of Tübingen. “In China, for example, new, higher-yielding rice varieties and other innovations were introduced in the 11th century [C.E.]. While the higher yields enabled the empire to remain the dominant power, they did not subsequently lead to a better standard of living for the general population. Instead, population density increased: People had more children because this was seen as a form of security in old age. This meant, however, that each individual had not more to eat, but less. And importantly the quality declined, for example, in terms of high-quality protein.”.

Europe’s findings on technology mirrored Asia’s. Improved technology helped support denser populations, but it didn’t increase average height or necessarily improve the nutritional value of food.

Industry observers note that going forward, the authors hope to link more of these changes in height to shifts in social conditions or developments in agriculture. “This requires further research,” noted Mark Hudson, an archaeologist at the Max Planck Institute of Geoanthropology. “However, the statistical data reveal trends and provide clues as to when these changes occurred.”.

His favorite interviews have included sit-downs with Roger Federer in Switzerland, Kobe Bryant in Los Angeles, and Tinker Hatfield in Portland.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

We reviewed every recommendation and added new apps for AI trip planning, eSIMs, flight tracking, budgeting, and travel safety.

Industry observers note that after travelling to more than 130 countries, we have used travel apps for everything from finding a last-minute room and navigating a city offline to translating menus, tracking flights and staying connected without paying ridiculous roaming charges. Some apps have earned a permanent place on our phones. Others have become outdated, overpriced or unnecessary.

For this 2026 guide, we cut through the clutter and chose the travel apps that solve real problems before and during a trip. You do not need to download every app on this list. Choose the ones that match your destination, travel style and the problems you are most likely to face.

The best travel apps for 2026 are Google Maps for navigation, Google Translate for language help, WhatsApp for communication, TripIt for organizing reservations, Google Flights for comparing airfare, Booking.com for hotels, Airalo or another destination-appropriate eSIM for mobile data, Uber for rides and AllTrails for hiking. Most travellers need only one or two apps from each category.

The Best Travel Apps for 2026 at a Glance.

Recent findings suggest that our picks are based on usefulness, ease of use, geographic coverage and whether the app solves a genuine travel problem. We have also included alternatives where the best choice depends on your destination.

Before getting into specialized apps, these are the five we would start with. They cover navigation, translation, communication, flight updates and trip organization.

Industry observers note that google Maps is still the app we use most often while travelling. It handles driving, walking and public-transit directions, lets us save hotels and restaurants, and shows opening hours, recent reviews and nearby services.

Before leaving reliable Wi-Fi, download the map for your destination. Offline maps are especially useful when you land without mobile data or drive through an area with poor reception. Keep in mind that live traffic, some transit information and certain search features may not work offline.

What we like: It combines navigation, trip planning and local research in one place.

What to know: Directions, opening hours and business listings are not always accurate. Double-check key information directly with the business.

Our verdict: Download it before almost any trip.

Sources indicate that google Translate has helped us order food, read signs and have simple conversations in places where we did not speak the language. You can type a phrase, speak into the phone or point the camera at text for an instant translation.

Download the languages you expect to use before your trip. That gives you a useful backup when you do not have data, although online translations can be more complete.

What we like: The camera function is incredibly useful for menus, ticket machines and signs.

What to know: Translations can be awkward or wrong, especially with slang, regional phrases and complicated instructions.

Our verdict: It is one of the most useful free international travel apps.

WhatsApp is the default communication tool in many parts of the world. Hotels, tour companies, drivers and local contacts often use it instead of standard text messages.

It supports individual and group chats, voice calls, video calls, photos, documents and live-location sharing over an internet connection. That makes it useful for keeping a travel group together or confirming a pickup without paying international texting charges.

What we like: It is widely used and keeps trip communication in one place.

What to know: It needs mobile data or Wi-Fi. Check the phone number carefully before sharing personal information or sending money.

Our verdict: Install it before leaving home and verify your number while you can still receive regular text messages.

Industry observers note that this may not be the most exciting recommendation, but it is one of the most practical. Download your airline’s official app before departure and sign in to your booking.

Airline apps can provide mobile check-in, boarding passes, gate notifications, delay information and rebooking options. During a disruption, the app may update before airport screens or email notifications do.

What we like: It gives you a direct line to the airline’s current information about your flight.

What to know: Push notifications are useful, but do not rely on them alone. Keep checking the departure board and listen for airport announcements.

Our verdict: Download it for every flight, even if you delete it after the trip.

In a recent development, tripIt turns confirmation emails into one organized itinerary. Forward your flight, hotel, rental-car and activity confirmations, and the app puts the details in chronological order.

According to recent reports, this is particularly useful on complicated trips with several flights, hotel changes or train journeys. Instead of searching through your inbox at a check-in desk, you can pull up the reservation in one place.

What we like: It reduces the chaos of juggling confirmation emails.

According to recent reports, what to know: Review imported details because automatic parsing is not infallible. Real-time alerts are generally part of the paid plan.

Our verdict: Best for multi-stop trips, business travel and anyone who likes everything organized.

Industry observers note that AI can be helpful for brainstorming routes, comparing neighbourhoods, creating packing lists and turning scattered ideas into a first-draft itinerary. It should not be treated as the final authority on visa rules, border requirements, prices, opening hours, transit schedules or safety alerts. Verify anything that could cost you money or prevent you from entering a country.

In a recent development, chatGPT is most useful when you give it real constraints: your travel dates, budget, interests, pace, mobility needs and where you are staying. It can then help turn those details into a practical first draft rather than a generic list of attractions.

Recent findings suggest that we also use AI to compare neighbourhoods, create checklists and identify questions we still need to research. The trick is to treat the result as a planning assistant, not a booking engine or government authority.

What we like: It is flexible and can promptly reorganize a complicated trip.

What to know: AI can produce outdated or invented information. Always confirm bookings, travel rules, prices and operating hours through official sources.

Our verdict: Excellent for planning and editing; unreliable as the sole source of truth.

Recent findings suggest that wanderlog combines itinerary planning, maps, reservations, notes and collaboration. It is useful for road trips and group travel because several people can add places and adjust the strategy.

Recent findings suggest that the visual map helps reveal when an itinerary makes no geographic sense. That sounds obvious, but it is remarkably easy to plan breakfast on one side of a city, lunch on the other and dinner back where you started.

What we like: The shared planning and map view make group trips easier.

What to know: A detailed itinerary can become cluttered. Keep some flexibility rather than scheduling every hour.

Our verdict: A strong choice for collaborative planning and road trips.

In a recent development, finding a cheap flight is only part of the job. These apps help us compare dates, monitor prices and track disruptions once the trip begins.

Google Flights is not a conventional downloadable app, but it remains one of the fastest ways to compare airfare. The calendar and price graph make it easy to see whether leaving a day earlier or using a nearby airport could reduce the fare.

Recent findings suggest that set a price alert when you are not ready to book. Google Flights sends updates when fares change, but you will usually complete the purchase with the airline or another booking provider.

What we like: It is fast, flexible and excellent for comparing dates.

It has been revealed that what to know: It does not show every airline or every possible fare. Compare the final price, baggage allowance and change rules before booking.

Our verdict: Our first stop for airfare research. Before pressing confirm, read our guide to airline booking traps that can make a cheap flight cost more.

Skyscanner is useful when you know you want to travel but have not settled on a destination. Its flexible search tools can surface options by month, country or broad destination.

Industry observers note that it also compares hotels and rental cars, although we mainly use it for flight discovery. Once you find a fare, pay close attention to whether the booking is through the airline or an online travel agency.

What we like: Flexible searches are ideal for travellers who can follow the deal.

It has been revealed that what to know: The cheapest result is not automatically the best one. Customer service and change policies vary by booking provider.

Our verdict: Best for inspiration and flexible travel dates.

Available on: iOS and supported Apple devices.

In a recent development, flighty turns a flight number into a detailed timeline with schedule changes, aircraft information and disruption updates. Frequent flyers appreciate how quickly it presents complicated flight information.

It is most useful on travel days, especially when weather or airport congestion starts knocking schedules sideways. The free version is enough for occasional travellers, while frequent flyers may value the paid alerts.

What we like: It presents flight changes clearly and can reduce airport uncertainty.

What to know: Some of its best features require a subscription, and platform availability may not suit every traveller.

Our verdict: A specialist app worth considering if you fly often.

Finding the right place to stay is about more than price. We look at location, recent reviews, cancellation policies, hidden fees, and whether the property actually suits the way we travel. These accommodation apps make it easier to compare hotels, apartments, hostels, and vacation rentals without bouncing between a dozen websites.

Booking.com remains one of the easiest places to compare a wide range of accommodation, from simple guesthouses to luxury hotels. The filters are especially useful when we need parking, a specific neighbourhood, breakfast, air conditioning or a refundable rate.

It has been revealed that read recent reviews rather than relying only on the overall score. We pay particular attention to comments about noise, cleanliness, construction and whether the room matches the photos.

What we like: Huge inventory and practical search filters.

Recent findings suggest that what to know: Cancellation and payment rules vary by property. Confirm whether taxes and resort fees are included before booking.

Our verdict: Our top general-purpose hotel app.

Airbnb is most useful when we want a kitchen, laundry, a living area or enough bedrooms for a group. It can also provide options in neighbourhoods with few conventional hotels.

Sources indicate that compare the total price rather than the nightly rate. Cleaning charges, service fees and local taxes can change the value swiftly. Read the house rules and cancellation policy before paying, and check whether the host has a substantial history of recent reviews.

What we like: It can provide more space and practical amenities than a hotel.

What to know: Quality is inconsistent, and fees can make a seemingly cheap stay expensive.

Our verdict: Best for longer stays and groups, not automatically the cheapest option.

Best for: Hostels, dorms, private rooms and social accommodation.

Price: Free to search; booking deposit or fees may apply.

Available on: iOS, Android and web.

Hostelworld makes it easy to compare hostels by location, room type, atmosphere and recent guest reviews. It is particularly useful for solo travellers who care about communal spaces and meeting other people.

Do not assume every hostel is a party hostel—or that every quiet-looking property will actually be quiet. Read recent reviews for comments about security, lockers, bathrooms, noise and the surrounding area.

What we like: It provides hostel-specific details that general hotel sites often miss.

Industry observers note that what to know: A low bed price can rise after taxes, linen fees or deposits. Check whether lockers require your own padlock.

Our verdict: The most useful specialist app for hostel travellers.

It has been revealed that there is no single eSIM provider that is cheapest or fastest in every country. Compare the local network, amount of high-speed data, hotspot rules, validity period and whether the proposal is data-only before buying.

Airalo makes it straightforward to buy and install an eSIM before a trip. You choose the destination, select a data package and follow the installation instructions on a compatible phone.

According to recent reports, we like that it removes the need to find a physical SIM card immediately after landing. Regional looks can also be convenient on multi-country trips, although a country-specific initiative may offer better value.

What we like: Easy setup and broad destination coverage.

What to know: Most plans are data-only, and the local network or speed can vary. Check phone compatibility before purchasing.

Our verdict: A convenient starting point for travellers newly introduced to eSIMs.

Ubigi is worth comparing with Airalo because eSIM value changes by country. In some destinations, one provider may offer a better local carrier, more data or a longer validity period.

Industry observers note that install the app and eSIM before departure whenever possible. Take screenshots of the setup instructions in case your connection disappears halfway through activation.

What we like: It gives travellers another established option instead of assuming one provider always wins.

Recent findings suggest that what to know: Coverage and value depend on the specific plan. Read the plan details rather than buying based only on the headline price.

Our verdict: Compare it destination by destination.

Getting around an unfamiliar city can be one of the most confusing parts of travel. These apps help us compare public transit, initiative longer connections, and arrange rides when trains or buses are not practical.

Citymapper can be easier to understand than a standard map when a city has several transit systems layered on top of one another. It compares routes, highlights transfers and often gives useful instructions about which station exit to use.

We find it particularly useful in large cities where choosing the wrong train direction or exit can add a surprising amount of time.

What we like: Clear transit directions and route comparisons.

What to know: Coverage is limited to supported cities, and live information depends on local transit data.

Our verdict: Excellent in cities where it is available.

According to recent reports, rome2Rio is useful during the early planning stage when you know where you want to go but not how to get there. Enter two places and it outlines possible combinations of flights, trains, buses, ferries and driving routes.

Sources indicate that we use it as a starting point rather than the final booking authority. Once we understand the route, we verify schedules and buy tickets directly from the transport operator whenever practical.

What we like: It makes complicated overland connections easier to visualize.

Sources indicate that what to know: Estimated times and prices can change. Confirm every important connection with the operator.

Our verdict: One of the best tools for answering, ‘How do we actually get there?’.

Sources indicate that uber can remove the uncertainty of explaining a destination, handling cash and negotiating a fare in an unfamiliar city. The app shows the route, vehicle and driver details before the ride begins.

Availability and regulations vary widely. In some destinations, another local app is more common, and airports may require pickup from a designated ride-hailing area.

What we like: Upfront trip details and cashless payment are convenient.

According to recent reports, what to know: Surge pricing can be expensive. Always confirm the licence plate and driver before getting into a vehicle.

Our verdict: Useful where it operates, but check the dominant local alternative.

Sources indicate that managing money abroad can get complicated swiftly. Exchange rates, foreign transaction fees, ATM charges, and shared expenses all add up, especially on longer trips or when travelling with other people. These apps help us understand what things really cost, manage different currencies, and keep track of who paid for what without turning dinner into an accounting meeting.

Industry observers note that wise lets eligible customers hold and exchange several currencies and spend with a linked card. It can be useful for frequent travellers, remote workers and anyone receiving money in more than one currency.

According to recent reports, always compare the total conversion cost with your regular bank or credit card. The best option depends on your country, card benefits and the type of transaction.

What we like: Transparent conversion information and multi-currency tools.

In a recent development, what to know: Availability, card features and fees vary by country. It is a financial service, so protect the account with strong security.

Our verdict: A useful tool for frequent international travellers.

XE is the app we open when a price full of unfamiliar zeros makes our brains quietly leave the room. It converts currencies quickly and helps you understand what a meal, taxi or hotel actually costs in your home currency.

Remember that the rate shown in a converter is not necessarily the rate your bank, ATM or exchange desk will give you after fees.

What we like: Fast, simple conversions.

What to know: It shows a reference rate, not a guaranteed retail exchange rate.

Our verdict: Keep it on your phone for quick price checks.

Industry observers note that splitwise prevents the end-of-trip ritual where everyone stares at a pile of receipts and suddenly forgets who paid for the rental car. Add shared expenses as you go, assign who owes what and let the app calculate the running balance.

It is particularly helpful for groups using different payment methods or taking turns covering major expenses.

What we like: It reduces awkward money conversations and messy arithmetic.

What to know: It records debts but does not automatically settle every balance. Agree on currencies and exchange rates at the beginning of the trip.

Our verdict: Essential for group trips.

According to recent reports, booking tours and activities in advance can save time, especially when popular attractions have timed entry or limited availability. We use these apps to compare tours, skip-the-line tickets, day trips, and local experiences, but we always check the operator, recent reviews, cancellation policy, and exactly what is included before booking.

According to recent reports, getYourGuide is useful when timed-entry tickets sell out or when a guided visit adds real context. It covers major attractions, walking tours, food tours, day trips and airport transfers in many popular destinations.

According to recent reports, read the cancellation policy and identify the actual tour operator before booking. A marketplace can list several versions of what looks like the same experience.

What we like: Strong inventory in major tourism destinations.

What to know: Quality depends on the local operator, not only the booking platform.

Our verdict: A good place to compare organized experiences.

Recent findings suggest that viator has a broad inventory of tours and activities around the world. We use it to see what is available, compare departure times and identify experiences that may be difficult to organize independently.

Sources indicate that as with any marketplace, read the newest reviews and check exactly what is included. A low starting price may refer to a basic option without transport, admission or the advertised upgrade.

What we like: It covers an enormous range of destinations and activities.

What to know: Listings from different operators can look very similar. Check inclusions, pickup details and cancellation terms.

Our verdict: Best for comparing a wide range of tours.

Finding the right trail or campsite takes more than choosing the prettiest photo. We look at distance, difficulty, recent trail conditions, offline map access, weather, and whether the route matches our experience level. These hiking, camping, and outdoor apps help us plan more confidently, but they should always be used alongside proper preparation and local safety information.

In a recent development, allTrails is an easy starting point for finding hikes by location, distance, difficulty and user rating. Recent reviews can reveal muddy sections, closures, parking problems and trail conditions that a static guidebook cannot.

In a recent development, download the route before leaving reception and carry a backup. A phone app is useful, but it does not replace proper preparation, weather awareness or a dedicated navigation tool in remote terrain.

What we like: It makes trail discovery accessible and provides recent user feedback.

According to recent reports, what to know: Crowdsourced routes can be inaccurate. Do not rely on a single phone app for serious backcountry navigation.

Our verdict: Best for day hikes and casual outdoor planning.

According to recent reports, gaia GPS is aimed at travellers who need more detail than a simple trail list. It supports topographic maps, route planning and map layers useful for hiking, camping and remote travel.

Recent findings suggest that learn how to use it before heading into the backcountry. Download the required maps, carry power and tell someone your route. Technology is helpful right up until the battery dies.

What we like: Detailed mapping and route-planning tools.

What to know: It has a learning curve, and vital map features may require a subscription.

Our verdict: Better suited to experienced outdoor travellers than casual city walkers.

The following apps can be excellent, but they are more specialized or depend heavily on your destination:.

Hidden-city ticketing involves booking a connecting itinerary and intentionally leaving at the connection instead of taking the final flight. It can violate airline conditions, makes checked baggage impractical and can cause the rest of an itinerary to be cancelled. We would not build a trip around it.

Price forecasts can be useful signals, but airfare and hotel prices remain unpredictable. Treat predictions as estimates, not promises. Book when the price, schedule and cancellation terms work for your trip.

Use apps to organize information, not to replace official immigration sources. Entry requirements can depend on nationality, residency, passport type, trip purpose and even transit airports.

According to recent reports, google Maps can provide offline driving navigation for downloaded areas, and Google Translate supports downloaded language packs. Outdoor apps such as AllTrails and Gaia GPS can offer offline maps depending on the plan. Save boarding passes, hotel addresses and reservation numbers before leaving Wi-Fi.

AI can build a useful first draft, but it should not be allowed to quietly invent your holiday. Use it to organize ideas, compare possible routes and identify questions. Then verify flights, hotels, opening hours, ticket rules, visa requirements and safety information through official or first-party sources.

According to recent reports, an eSIM can be useful when your regular carrier charges high roaming fees. Compare the local network, data allowance, hotspot rules and validity period before purchasing.

Which travel apps work without internet?

According to recent reports, google Maps and Google Translate support downloaded offline content. Some hiking apps provide offline maps through paid looks. Download everything before leaving reliable Wi-Fi.

It has been revealed that the best travel app is not the one with the longest feature list. It is the one that solves a problem at the moment you need it. For us, Google Maps, Google Translate, WhatsApp, an airline app and an itinerary organizer cover the basics. From there, we add an eSIM, flight tracker, budgeting app or hiking map depending on the trip.

It has been revealed that download your essentials before leaving home, test that you can sign in and save critical information offline. Then put the phone away once in a while. The app is supposed to help you experience the trip—not become the trip.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, carnival Cruise Line aims to introduce a new class of ships to its fleet.
  • The tech giant said the fresh ships were intentionally designed on a smaller scale.
  • “With a 29-ship fleet, we know our guests appreciate choices,” said Christine Duffy, president of Carnival Cruise Line.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a recent development, carnival Cruise Line aims to introduce a new class of ships to its fleet. Two LNG-powered ships of approximately 130,000 gross tons each will be built by Fincantieri for delivery in 2033 and 2035, according to a press release.

The tech giant said the fresh ships were intentionally designed on a smaller scale. That will give them access to more ports and widen the brand’s destination and itinerary options.

“With a 29-ship fleet, we know our guests appreciate choices,” said Christine Duffy, president of Carnival Cruise Line.

“They love the incredible experiences and amenities on our Excel Class ships, the largest in our fleet, but they also love the intimacy our smaller ships offer. This upcoming class gives us the best of both worlds, helping future-proof our fleet with the flexibility to take America’s Cruise Line to even more places in the years ahead.”.

At the New York event on Thursday, Duffy also gave a first look at the upcoming Carnival Destiny. She outlined expansions at Celebration Key and RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay, and announced looks to extend popular onboard benefits ashore.

Industry observers note that the Carnival Destiny will debut in 2029 as the first of three Ace Class ships. It will have more outdoor pools than any other Carnival ship: eight in total, including six infinity pools, with more than 11,200 square feet of water surface. They include the brand’s first outward-facing main pool zone.

Other features include an ocean-front lanai with several pools and dining and bar venues near the sea. There will also be upcoming premium venues with multideck ocean views, including an exclusive pool on Deck 18 Aft. The ship will offer 25 new dining and bar experiences and a reimagined Limelight Lounge.

In a recent development, compared with Carnival’s newest ships, the Carnival Destiny will have nearly twice the space for family venues and attractions. They will be grouped in a single family zone with mini golf, arcades and dining. A new Dr. Seuss Splash Station will build on Carnival’s 13-year partnership with Dr. Seuss Enterprises.

Recent findings suggest that for adults, the ship will introduce Carnival’s first adult-only zone. It will span four decks and include the brand’s first adult-only staterooms, an expanded Serenity retreat and an exclusive rooftop pool deck.

Carnival is also planning two expansion phases at Celebration Key, each adding 3,000 guests of land-side capacity, for 6,000 in total.

In a recent development, the first phase is due in 2028. It will add a new portal with a heated beach-entry pool and swim-up bar, a social waterslide for four to five riders and an aqua play area for younger children.

Industry observers note that the second phase, in 2030, will bring a major water park with 18 waterslides. It will also have what the organization called the cruise industry’s longest lazy river, plus an exclusive area with an infinity pool, more beach access and fresh dining and bar concepts.

It has been revealed that in spring 2027, Carnival will open Serenity Beach at RelaxAway, Half Moon Cay. It will be a complimentary retreat for guests 21 and older, with daybeds and cabanas available for an extra charge.

It has been revealed that starting in February 2027, Carnival’s CHEERS!, CHEERS! Zero Proof, Bottomless Bubbles and CHEERS! Social drink packages will also apply at Celebration Key and RelaxAway.

“Guests are seeking more choice, more flexibility and more ways to make the most of their time together,” Duffy mentioned.

In a press release, the tech giant said guest feedback plays a significant role in the awards, with winning tours and operators achieving exceptional satisfaction scores and consistently demonstrating a strong commitment to quality throughout the guest journey.

The 2026 awards highlighted responsible tourism and the importance of strong destination partnerships, MSC added.

#19595. Senate Republicans lament midterms, weigh leadership election delay

Senate Republicans lament midterms, weigh leadership election delay

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (564 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Rollcall

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday.
  • Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.
  • But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the new Congress.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Senate Majority Leader John Thune arrives for a GOP conference meeting at the Capitol on Tuesday. (Tom Williams/CQ Roll Call).

Senate Republicans on Tuesday were weighing whether to postpone their leadership elections after what several senators described as a “frank” conversation about their midterm losses last week.

But so far, no official candidate has emerged to challenge John Thune, R-S.D., for the post of minority leader in the new Congress.

The conference was supposed to begin its leadership elections Tuesday morning, but pushed those back to hear from members still reeling from the midterm results, which saw the GOP lose their Senate majority. As the conference meeting turned into what some dubbed an “open-mic session,” they took a break to attend previously scheduled committee hearings, with a proposal to return at 2 p.m. Next they must decide whether to forge ahead and pick leaders Tuesday or to punt those choices to a different day.

Sen. Josh Hawley, R-Mo., noted the conversation taking place was “honest” and “frank.”.

“I will vote for the delay,” he said. “We’ve got a lot of things that we’ve got to think through, and I think to rush into this and to just ratify all the same leadership — I mean, what message does that send?”.

“If you don’t think after losing seven seats minimum that we need to change course, I don’t know what planet you’re on,” he said, adding he was frustrated that his party didn’t do more to focus on topics like affordability ahead of the midterms. “I know it’s easy to blame other people, but we need to look at what has happened here.”.

Sen. Ron Johnson, R-Wis., who is leading the charge to delay the leadership elections and collected signatures to call the conference meeting beforehand, called it “a very high-quality conversation” in which he was “leading.”.

“People are voicing opinions on all sides of the challenges. It’s one of those times in the Republican conference where you kind of go, ‘We’ve got some smart people, and we’re having a very good, respectful conversation.’”.

In a recent development, no challenger to Thune, the current majority leader, stepped forward during the closed-door meeting, several senators stated. Sen. Kevin Cramer, R-N.D., said “they’re not even criticizing Thune” inside the room. “It hasn’t been about John Thune.”.

“It’s been about the family,” Cramer said, describing it as a “family discussion.” Thune and others in leadership had yet to speak, as the candidate forum hadn’t started yet.

Sen. Rand Paul, R-Ky., said voters reacted to high gas prices, the war in Iran and the cost of living.

Recent findings suggest that “The cost of living defeated us,” Paul remarked. “I don’t think anybody in Texas who voted for the Democrat governor was voting against John Thune. If you diagnose that as a problem, you’re misdiagnosing the problem.”.

According to recent reports, hawley didn’t say how long he’d like to see a delay. “Long enough for people to think through this, and if there’s somebody else … or several somebodies who want to run for positions, let them think through it.”.

Cramer was asked if senators in the room were placing any blame on President Donald Trump over how he handled midterm messaging.

“There was a lot of discussion about the president,” Cramer noted.
